midterm

1.Introduction: Background:The board crossing has always been a important work of a country, as the time goes by, there surely have some changes in the types people use to cross, the location where people crossing, so know how this will change and thus make some measures to better handle this work is necessary.The Bureau of Transportation Statistics (BTS) Border Crossing Data provide summary statistics for inbound crossings at the U.S.-Canada and the U.S.-Mexico border at the port level. Data are available for trucks, trains, containers, buses, personal vehicles, passengers, and pedestrians. Border crossing data are collected at ports of entry by U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP). The data reflect the number of vehicles, containers, passengers, and pedestrians entering the United States through CBP facilities. CBP does not collect comparable data on outbound crossings. BTS also does not collect data about the size or number of seats per bus. The dataset “Border.csv” has the data of border crossing from Jan 1966 to Aug 2025, throught this dataset we can visualize some question”How is change between different border after the time period”“which type of measure do people takes to cross the board.” Thus the governors will know how to manage the work.

border <- read.csv("C:/Users/27753/Desktop/PM566/Border.csv")

2.Data preparation: how and where the data were acquired: “In the list of suggestion”->“Bureau of Transportation Statistics”on the Health and Biological data part->“Border Crossing Data” on the Statistical Products and Data: A-F part -> view full database here. Then the whole data could be downloaded and analyzed. clean and wrangle data: From the dataset, there are some measures to handle the dataset first: 1.Handle Missing Values:State, Latitude, Longitude, and Point have 4 missing values — it can be droped . 2.Fix Value Column:Convert from string (e.g., “450,639”) to integer (450639), in order to make comparison in the next step. 3.Parse Date:Extract date information and add two columns “Year” and “Month”(in order to make comparison eaiser as well)

library(tidyverse)

library(lubridate)
library(stringr)
# --- Data Cleaning & Wrangling ---
# Check and count missing values per variable
border %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ sum(is.na(.)), .names = "na_{col}"))
  na_Port.Name na_State na_Port.Code na_Border na_Date na_Measure na_Value
1            0        0            0         0       0          0        0
  na_Latitude na_Longitude na_Point
1           4            4        0
# 1. Handle missing values
border <- border %>%
  drop_na(State, Latitude, Longitude, Point)

# 2. Clean the 'Value' column (remove commas and convert to numeric)
border <- border %>%
  mutate(Value = as.numeric(gsub(",", "", Value)))

# 3. Convert 'Date' column (e.g., "Aug 2025") to proper date and extract Year/Month
border <- border %>%
  mutate(
    month = str_extract(Date, "^[A-Za-z]+"),
    Year = str_extract(Date, "\\d{4}"),
    Year = as.numeric(Year),
    # change the month variable from string to integer
    month = str_to_title(month),
    temp_date = paste(month, Year),
    temp_date = my(temp_date),
    month = month(temp_date)
  ) %>%
  select(-temp_date)

After the clean and prep, there is no values in the table so the analysis could be more precise. The data in the “Value” variable all turn to numeric so the next step we may be can analysis such question like “find the maximum 10 or minimum 10 place in a certain year”, The “Date” variable also separate into two variable” month” and “year”, which can help us better locate when is time of the certain data we want to search.

3.Exploratory Analysis:step checking the data and cleaning the data is down on step 2

library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

# 1. dataset characteristics and variables included
colnames(border)
 [1] "Port.Name" "State"     "Port.Code" "Border"    "Date"      "Measure"  
 [7] "Value"     "Latitude"  "Longitude" "Point"     "month"     "Year"     
cat("Number of rows:", nrow(border), "\n")
Number of rows: 403853 
cat("Number of columns:", ncol(border), "\n")
Number of columns: 12 
# --- Summary by Year and Border Type ---
yearly_summary <- border %>%
  group_by(Year, Border) %>%
  summarise(
    Total_Value = sum(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
    Mean_Value = mean(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
    Median_Value = median(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD_Value = sd(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

The table shows the dataset charactistics, these are 12 variables after the clean and prep. And the list shows, there are only mexico and Canada Border. For me, I want to figure the relationship between the value(numbers of people to cross the board) location,time and measure, so the “Value” ” Lattitude” “Longitude”“year”“month”(may only use year)“Measure” are the key variables I want to use. Because the value could differ much considering the measure, analyze distribution directly has no meanings For the distribution fo key variables, I want to first analysis the sum of people each year categoried by the border and see the distribution of board crossing numbers over year.

library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

# --- 1. Aggregate total crossings per year and border ---
yearly_border_people <- border %>%
  group_by(Year, Border) %>%
  summarise(Total_People = sum(Value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(Year)

# --- 2. Histogram (bar chart) by border ---
ggplot(yearly_border_people, aes(x = factor(Year), y = Total_People, fill = Border)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge", alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("US-Canada Border" = "#1f77b4", "US-Mexico Border" = "#ff7f0e")) +
  labs(
    title = "Total People Crossing Each Border by Year",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Total Crossings (Sum of Value)",
    fill = "Border Type"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
  )
# --- 3. Show the same data in a clean table ---
yearly_border_people %>%
  mutate(Total_People = comma(Total_People)) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Border, values_from = Total_People) %>%
  kable(
    caption = "Total People Crossing Each Border by Year",
    align = "c",
    format = "html"
  ) %>%
 kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, bootstrap_options = c("hover", "striped", "condensed"))

I also want to find the relationship between measure and value, the plot will show how many type in “Measure”, and show the num of people who use this measure at year 2025

library(tidyverse)
library(scales)

# --- 1. Count how many unique Measure types ---
num_measure_types <- border %>%
  distinct(Measure) %>%
  nrow()

cat("Number of unique Measure types:", num_measure_types, "\n")
Number of unique Measure types: 12 
# --- 2. Filter for year 2025 and summarize totals by Measure and Border ---
measure_2025 <- border %>%
  filter(Year == 2025) %>%
  group_by(Border, Measure) %>%
  summarise(Total_People = sum(Value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(Border, desc(Total_People))

# --- 3. make plot
mexico_plot <- measure_2025 %>%
  filter(Border == "US-Mexico Border") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(Measure, Total_People), y = Total_People, fill = Measure)) +
  geom_col(alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Mexico(2025)",
    x = "Measure Type",
    y = "Total People"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    legend.position = "none"
  )


canada_plot <- measure_2025 %>%
  filter(Border == "US-Canada Border") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(Measure, Total_People), y = Total_People, fill = Measure)) +
  geom_col(alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Canada(2025)",
    x = "Measure Type",
    y = "Total People"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +

    legend.position = "none"
  )

mexico_plot + canada_plot

It can been seen that there are 12 unique types of transportation to cross the board, and the plot could show that personal vehicles passengers counts for the most in both two board, but from the third most type, the two board start to look different, this may due to different development of local transportation and that need further research.Governors could make inspects works relevant to that number of each type. More analysis about the relationship, it should go to the Preliminary Results part. 4.Preliminary Results: use the lattitude and longtitude, we can visualize the frequency of value on the map to compare the change in 1997 to 2024(these years has the longest period and complete data for a whole year)

library(tidyverse)
library(leaflet)
library(scales)

# --- 1. visualize the frequency of value on the map
location_summary <- border %>%
  group_by(Year, State, Port.Name, Latitude, Longitude) %>%
  summarise(Total_People = sum(Value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
location_1997 <- location_summary %>% filter(Year == 1997)
location_2024 <- location_summary %>% filter(Year == 2024)
pal <- colorNumeric(palette = "YlOrRd", domain = location_summary$Total_People)
map_1997 <- leaflet(location_1997) %>%
  addTiles() %>%
  addCircleMarkers(
    lng = ~Longitude,
    lat = ~Latitude,
    radius = ~sqrt(Total_People) / 200, # Scale circle size by volume
    color = ~pal(Total_People),
    stroke = FALSE,
    fillOpacity = 0.8,
    popup = ~paste0(
      "<b>Port:</b> ", Port.Name, "<br>",
      "<b>State:</b> ", State, "<br>",
      "<b>Total People (1997):</b> ", comma(Total_People)
    )
  ) %>%
  addLegend(
    pal = pal,
    values = ~Total_People,
    title = "Total People (1997)",
    position = "bottomright"
  )
map_2024 <- leaflet(location_2024) %>%
  addTiles() %>%
  addCircleMarkers(
    lng = ~Longitude,
    lat = ~Latitude,
    radius = ~sqrt(Total_People) / 200,
    color = ~pal(Total_People),
    stroke = FALSE,
    fillOpacity = 0.8,
    popup = ~paste0(
      "<b>Port:</b> ", Port.Name, "<br>",
      "<b>State:</b> ", State, "<br>",
      "<b>Total People (2024):</b> ", comma(Total_People)
    )
  ) %>%
  addLegend(
    pal = pal,
    values = ~Total_People,
    title = "Total People (2024)",
    position = "bottomright"
  )

#  Display with kable
location_summary <- border %>%
  filter(Year %in% c(1997, 2024)) %>%
  group_by(Year, State, Port.Name, Latitude, Longitude) %>%
  summarise(Total_People = sum(Value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

location_summary <- border %>%
  filter(Year %in% c(1997, 2024)) %>%
  group_by(Year, State, Port.Name, Latitude, Longitude) %>%
  summarise(Total_People = sum(Value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")


location_summary <- border %>%
  filter(Year %in% c(1997, 2024)) %>%
  group_by(Year, State, Port.Name, Latitude, Longitude) %>%
  summarise(Total_People = sum(Value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

location_comparison <- location_summary %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Year,
    values_from = Total_People,
    values_fill = 0
  ) %>%
  rename(Total_1997 = `1997`, Total_2024 = `2024`) %>%
  # Exclude any rows with 0 in either year
  filter(Total_1997 > 0, Total_2024 > 0) %>%
  mutate(
    Change = Total_2024 - Total_1997,
    Percent_Change = (Change / Total_1997) * 100
  )

top_increases <- location_comparison %>%
  arrange(desc(Percent_Change)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 10)

top_decreases <- location_comparison %>%
  arrange(Percent_Change) %>%
  slice_head(n = 10)
format_table <- function(data, title) {
  data %>%
    mutate(
      Total_1997 = comma(Total_1997),
      Total_2024 = comma(Total_2024),
      Change = comma(Change),
      Percent_Change = paste0(round(Percent_Change, 1), "%")
    ) %>%
    select(Port.Name, State, Total_1997, Total_2024, Change, Percent_Change) %>%
    kable(
      caption = title,
      align = "c",
      format = "html",
      col.names = c("Port Name", "State", "Total (1997)", "Total (2024)", "Change", "% Change")
    ) %>%
    kable_styling(
      full_width = FALSE,
      bootstrap_options = c("hover", "striped", "condensed")
    )
}
format_table(top_increases, "Top 10 Locations with the Largest Percentage Increases in Border Crossings (1997 → 2024, Excluding Zeros)")

Lastly, I want to check whether the value would differ between different month, this could tell which month should be distributed more employees.

library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)

# make the plot
border <- border %>%
  filter(Year >= 1997, Year <= 2024, Value > 0) %>%
  mutate(Month = as.numeric(month))
monthly_total <- border %>%
  group_by(Month) %>%
  summarise(Total_Value = sum(Value, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup()
ggplot(monthly_total, aes(x = factor(Month), y = Total_Value, fill = factor(Month))) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "magma") +
  labs(
    title = "Total Number of People Crossing by Month (All Years Combined)",
    x = "Month",
    y = "Total Crossings"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold")
  )
monthly_total_summary <- border %>%
  mutate(Month = as.numeric(month)) %>%
  group_by(Month) %>%
  summarise(Total_Value = sum(Value, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  arrange(desc(Total_Value)) %>%
  mutate(
    Month = month.abb[Month]  # Convert numeric month to abbreviation
  )

# --- Display with kable ---
monthly_total_summary %>%
  kable(
    caption = "Total Border Crossings by Month (All Years Combined, Arranged by Total)",
    col.names = c("Month", "Total Crossings"),
    format = "html",
    digits = 0,
    align = c("c", "r")
  ) %>%
  kable_styling(
    bootstrap_options = c("hover", "striped", "condensed"),
    full_width = FALSE,
    position = "center"
  ) %>%
  column_spec(1, bold = TRUE, color = "white", background = "#2c3e50") %>%
  column_spec(2, background = "#ecf0f1")

5.conclusion In order to know the border crossing condition of recent 30 years, I use the data from the Bureau of Transprtation websites to do some analysis and visualization. The location,measure to cross, time and value could serve as key variables to analysis the relationship between them, there several changes in the value for each boarding location throught the year and there are also some measure and value difference between Maxico and Canada border that show the trend of this two borders. But doubtly, the crossing people did not show any trend like travellers did in month distribution so further reasearch of each measure might could be done.
